title: Missing Files / Pressure List
mission: Show what is still hidden, gated, redacted, unreviewed, unverified, missing, or waiting for counter-source before the site can upgrade claims.
boundary: A missing file is not proof of a cover-up by itself. It is a pressure point: a record needed to prove, disprove, classify, downgrade, or verify a claim. No private victim identifiers, explicit content, private addresses, family/minor data or live movement data.

items.title: First 10 United States v. Epstein PDFs
items.whyItMatters: These PDFs are the first court-record files queued from the official DOJ United States v. Epstein page. They may contain charging records, motions, orders, exhibits, correspondence or unrelated docket material, but that cannot be known until file-level review occurs.
items.whatWouldProve: Record type, docket purpose, date, parties, and whether any safe non-sensitive fact can become a Verified Record Card.
items.whatItCannotProveYet: Any file-level allegation, name mention, exhibit content or conclusion before the PDFs are opened and safely classified.
items.nextAction: Manual age-verified review; classify each file as indictment/motion/order/exhibit/transcript/correspondence/other.

items.title: First 10 United States v. Maxwell PDFs
items.whyItMatters: These PDFs are the first Maxwell court-record files queued from the official DOJ page. The case has a confirmed criminal lane, but the file contents still require classification before use.
items.whatWouldProve: Whether the file is a charging record, motion, order, exhibit, sentencing/verdict-related record, appeal item or other docket material.
items.whatItCannotProveYet: Specific file contents or named allegations before review.
items.nextAction: Manual age-verified review; create verified cards only from safe non-sensitive record summaries.

items.title: USVI v. JPMorgan first PDF set
items.whyItMatters: The banking/compliance lane cannot be upgraded from source-route phase until the PDFs are classified into complaint, motion, order, exhibit, settlement, dismissal, correspondence or other material.
items.whatWouldProve: The actual legal posture and document type of each filing, including whether it contains allegations, orders, settlement terms, denials or exhibits.
items.whatItCannotProveYet: Banking wrongdoing, compliance failure, knowledge, settlement meaning or no-admission language without the record text.
items.nextAction: Open and classify first ten USVI v. JPMorgan PDFs; attach public response/no-admission language where present.

items.title: FOIA CBP lane
items.whyItMatters: Customs and Border Protection records may be relevant to historical travel, border, transport or logistics context, but the category needs separate safe review.
items.whatWouldProve: Official FOIA record categories, dates, document types and whether any safe historical transport evidence exists.
items.whatItCannotProveYet: Passenger identity, travel purpose, live movement or wrongdoing without specific records.
items.nextAction: Create FOIA-CBP scan batch; classify records as route index, exhibit, report, correspondence or privacy-blocked.

items.title: FOIA FBI lane
items.whyItMatters: FBI FOIA materials may contain investigation records, but each file must be handled by record type and redaction boundary.
items.whatWouldProve: Official investigation-record categories, dates and file types.
items.whatItCannotProveYet: Complete investigative knowledge, hidden records or unredacted facts.
items.nextAction: Create FBI FOIA scan batch and separate primary records from redacted/withheld/partial materials.

items.title: FOIA BOP lane
items.whyItMatters: Bureau of Prisons records are central to custody/death timeline questions, but they must be separated from speculation and handled through official records.
items.whatWouldProve: Official BOP file types, custody/death record routes and redaction limits.
items.whatItCannotProveYet: Any theory beyond what the documents state.
items.nextAction: Create BOP FOIA scan batch; classify record types and link any official OIG/custody records.

items.title: Florida public-record lane
items.whyItMatters: Florida records are a major historical legal lane, but need separation from federal case files and later disclosures.
items.whatWouldProve: State-level public-record routes, case materials, dates and legal posture.
items.whatItCannotProveYet: Federal case findings or unrelated institutional claims.
items.nextAction: Create Florida records scan batch; separate state court records, public records, correspondence and redactions.

items.title: Public denials / responses for named people
items.whyItMatters: Every people card needs a response/counter-source lane before claims can be responsibly upgraded. Silence, denial, correction and admission must be tracked separately.
items.whatWouldProve: What a named person publicly denied, corrected, admitted or clarified.
items.whatItCannotProveYet: Truth or falsity of the response by itself.
items.nextAction: Create public response cards for the first 20 Tracker Core people.

items.title: Foundation and nonprofit filings for institution lanes
items.whyItMatters: Institution and foundation lanes are only useful if Form 990, grant records, public statements and policy changes are attached.
items.whatWouldProve: Officer names, grants, recipients, program statements and institutional money routes where publicly filed.
items.whatItCannotProveYet: Improper influence or motive without additional records.
items.nextAction: Pull Form 990 and grant records for priority foundation lanes.

items.title: Redaction taxonomy
items.whyItMatters: A redaction is not automatically suspicious, but redaction type matters: court rule, protective order, victim-rights statute, personal identifiers, agency redaction, prior source redaction or privacy block.
items.whatWouldProve: Which redaction rules or explanations apply to different source categories.
items.nextAction: Build redaction taxonomy cards and attach them to scan/exposé pages.

items.title: Fake / falsely submitted material queue
items.whyItMatters: DOJ warned that public-submission material may include fake or falsely submitted material. Viral claims must be quarantined unless tied to primary records.
items.whatWouldProve: Which claims or files are primary records, public submissions, corrected, rejected, debunked or unverified.
items.whatItCannotProveYet: The truth of a viral claim without a primary record.
items.nextAction: Create fake-submission/counter-source queue and downgrade unsupported claims to X.

items.title: Search reliability warning attached to every scan
items.whyItMatters: DOJ warns search may be unreliable for handwritten or poorly formatted materials. Auto scans cannot replace manual review.
items.whatWouldProve: That index-level automation can detect file IDs and changes, but cannot guarantee content discovery.
items.whatItCannotProveYet: That no relevant content exists simply because search missed it.
items.nextAction: Attach search-reliability warning to auto pipeline, scan pages and missing-file board.
